notes: What can happen to a ship on the way. An event is rolled at the moment the
ship crosses from one world's reach into another's — the one place on a
voyage where something is already changing — and never anywhere else. The
rules under `rules` bound how often: `chance` is the roll on each crossing,
and there is at most one event between one docking and the next, so a long
road with six crossings on it is not six interruptions. Nothing here fires
while Uncle Theo is still teaching.
The `rules` block:
chance   required. 0..1. The chance a crossing turns into an event, before
eligibility: a crossing where nothing in the table fits stays quiet.
An event record:
id       required. Unique, lower case, no spaces. A save holds it.
title    required. What the card is called.
weight   optional, default 1. How often this one comes up against the
others that fit the same crossing. Each time a ship has seen an
event its weight is halved, so a long game meets the whole table.
when     optional. What has to be true for it to fit:
regions      [ inner | home | belt | outer | deep ] — the region
of the reach being crossed; leave it out for anywhere
carrying     [ good ids or categories ] — any of them aboard
notCarrying  [ good ids or categories ] — none of them aboard
coldCargo    true — something aboard that needs the cold hold
debt         true — the harbour bank is owed something
hull         true — the hull is worse than sound
text     required. What is happening, said to the captain.
choices  required, at least one. [{ label, requires, text, effects, outcomes }]
label     required. The button.
requires  optional. What the choice needs; without it the button
is there but greyed, with the reason on it:
dv         km/s in the tank
money      in the purse
holdUnits  free room in the hold
text      what happened, once chosen. Required unless `outcomes`.
effects   what it did. Optional; a choice may be only a story.
outcomes  optional, instead of text + effects: a list of
{ when, weight, text, effects }, one of which is rolled
when the event comes up (so a save cannot re-roll it).
`when` is { key: <a fitted key, e.g. tempControl> }.
If any outcome's `when` holds, the draw is among those
alone; otherwise it is among the ones without a `when`.
Effects, all optional, applied together:
money    a number (+ earns, − costs), or { fraction, of, cap } where `of` is
purse | cargo | contraband (the value aboard of that kind). A cost
never takes more than sixty hundredths of the purse: nothing in
this game costs a save.
dv       km/s of fuel, + or −. Never below empty.
rep      { emberkin | otter | cat | frog | here: ±n }. `here` is the people
whose region the crossing was in, for a stranger's gratitude.
cargo    { take: <good id or category> }  everything of that kind aboard
{ take: <good id>, qty: n }          that many
{ takeCold: <fraction> }              of what needs the cold hold
{ give: <good id>, qty: n }          put aboard (see holdUnits)
Consigned crates — somebody's errand — are never taken.
hull     ±n grades. − mends, + damages; never past failing.
debt     { pay: <fraction of the purse> } or { add: <fraction of the debt> }
Text may use {amount} for the money an effect moved, {cargo} for what a
cargo effect took or gave, and {here} for the people of the region.
The tone is the game's: nothing here is a trap, nothing is a fight, and the
worst outcome costs coin, crates or fuel — never the ship and never the save.

events.title: A Veyra hull comes alongside
events.text: A house warship of Veyra matches your road without asking and puts a scan through the hold, deck by deck. A steward's voice, very polite, says that the crest on some of your crates does not match the crest on their paperwork, because there is no paperwork.

choices.label: Hand the crates over and pay the fine
choices.text: They take {cargo} and {amount} besides, write it all down, and leave you the rest with a receipt. Somebody on Veyra will read that receipt.

choices.label: Insist they are salvage, and keep them

outcomes.text: The steward looks at the scan, looks at you, and decides that today it is salvage. The warship falls away. You have been noted.
The steward has heard salvage before. They take {cargo} and {amount} for the trouble of listening, and note the hull number twice.

choices.label: Burn away before the scan finishes
choices.text: Half a kilometre a second, spent all at once, and the scan loses you in the noise. The warship does not follow. Veyra will remember the road you took.

events.title: A Veyra hull comes alongside
events.text: A house warship of Veyra matches your road and scans the hold, deck by deck, without asking. A steward's voice thanks you for your patience, with a courtesy that cost nothing and was meant.

choices.label: Carry on
choices.text: They find what you found: cargo, honestly come by. The hull number goes in a book anyway.

events.title: A courier's wager
events.text: An Emberkin courier pulls alongside, close enough to read your name off the hull, and proposes a race to whichever harbour you are both bound for. There is a stake. There is always a stake.

outcomes.text: You fly it clean and arrive with the courier still a burn behind. She pays up on the dock and writes your name down, which is how the Emberkin say well done.
She was never racing you; she was racing her own timetable, and it was a good one. You pay up on the dock. She writes your name down anyway.

choices.label: Decline, politely
choices.text: She shrugs, which takes her about half a second, and is gone. Nothing is owed.

events.title: The Lamp flares
events.text: The Lamp throws a flare. The whole sky goes white on the instruments for a minute, and the thermometer in the hold starts to climb.

choices.label: Turn the hull to shade the hold
choices.text: Two hundred metres a second of turning and holding, and the crates sit in the ship's own shadow until the sky is quiet. Nothing aboard so much as sweats.

outcomes.text: The cold hold does what a cold hold is for. You watch the gauge, and it does not move.
Half of what was cold is not any more. {cargo}: soup, or near enough.

events.title: A beacon on the road
events.text: A beacon on the road ahead, thin and patient: a lighter with a dry tank, drifting the way you are going. They ask for whatever you can spare.

choices.label: Spare them a little fuel
choices.text: You hand across three hundred metres a second and their engine lights. {here} will tell this story with your ship's name in it.

choices.label: Keep what you have
choices.text: You call it in to the nearest harbour instead. Somebody will come, later, at their own pace. Nobody blames a small tank.

events.title: Somebody in the hold
events.text: A frog pilgrim is sitting in the hold. Nobody saw her come aboard and she does not say when. She would like to go wherever you are going, and she has a bead for every day she has been away.

choices.label: Take her along
choices.text: She pays her way in coin at the lock, hums for most of the crossing, and gives you a bead on the way out. It has been somewhere now.

choices.label: Put her off at the nearest raft
choices.text: She goes without a word, which from a frog is a very long word. The hold feels bigger, and worse.

events.title: A crate on the road
events.text: A crate on your road, tumbling slowly, with Nail's stencil on it and nobody's name. It will pass within a hundred metres.

choices.label: Bring it aboard
choices.text: A sheet of somebody's ship, straightened and stacked, and now yours: {cargo}. The cats would say it fell off a truck, if there were trucks.

choices.label: Leave it for the next ship
choices.text: It tumbles on. Somebody at Nail is already counting it lost.

events.title: A mechanic's opinion
events.text: A cat cutter matches your speed, and a mechanic looks your hull over from ten metres off, sucks her teeth, and offers to sort the worst of it for what is in your pocket.

choices.label: Let her
choices.text: Forty minutes, most of it her telling you what you did wrong, and the hull is a grade better than it was. She will remember your answer for years.

choices.label: Thank her and go on
choices.text: She shrugs, which is a whole sentence in cat, and drops away. The dent stays.

events.title: The bank's pennant
events.text: A launch with the Tassel harbour bank's pennant on it hails you the moment you are in the open, which is the moment they can.

choices.label: Pay something off now
choices.text: You hand over {amount} against what is owed. The clerk enters it twice and thanks you once.

choices.label: Not now
choices.text: The clerk notes that you said not now, and the interest notes it too.

events.title: A note to carry
events.text: A Glass scholar's skiff crosses your road and asks, over the radio and without preamble, whether you would carry a recording to wherever you are going. It is thirty years long. It is one note.

choices.label: Take it
choices.text: It weighs nothing and plays quietly the whole way. By the time you dock you can hum it, which the scholar said would happen.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: The skiff goes on its way. The note goes on without you.

events.title: A letter from the raft
events.text: A raft relay passes on a letter from Aunt Nellie. It is mostly about the weather, and it asks whether you are eating.

choices.label: Write back
choices.text: You write back that you are eating. It is not entirely true, and she will know.

choices.label: Read it twice and fold it away
choices.text: You keep it in the pocket where the pebble was. The weather on Tassel, it turns out, is fine.

events.title: A cat with advice
events.text: A cat cutter shadows you for a while, then hails to say, kindly, that your road through the rocks is the one everybody flies, and that there is a better one, for a consideration.

choices.label: Pay for the road
choices.text: The road she draws you saves nothing you can measure and a great deal you can feel. She takes {amount} and is gone before you can ask her name.

choices.label: Fly the road everybody flies
choices.text: She wishes you a quiet crossing, which is what cats say instead of goodbye, and peels off toward Nail.
